newsitem.title: USA: Ferber sentencing delayed from Dec 18 to Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: Ferber sentencing delayed from Dec 18 to Dec 19.

text.p: A federal judge has again delayed sentencing of former Lazard Frere & Co executive Mark Ferber, from December 18th to 19th, a Ferber lawyer said.

Kathy Weinman, a partner with Dwyer & Collora in Boston, said U.S. District Court Judge William Young wants an extra day, the 18th, to hear lawyers' views on how he should apply complicated federal sentencing guidelines to Ferber's case.
A federal jury on August 9 convicted Ferber on 58 of 61 counts of corruption and fraud concerning a $1 million fee-splitting arrangement with Merrill Lynch & Co. involving swap deals.
Ferber originally was scheduled for sentencing on Nov. 4. The date was delayed until Novermber 21, and then December 18.
Ferber faces a maximum sentence of five years for each of the 58 counts, or 290 years. But legal experts say he is unlikely to receive anything close to that amount.
